title: Cold-Plunge Season Starts Now
why: Seasonal for Portland locals: the Columbia is cooling from the 60s toward 42 degrees; October is the on-ramp.
hook_options: The river is getting colder. Good.
This is the stretch regulars wait for.
October is the on-ramp to 42 degrees.
caption: Summer water sat in the 60s. By January the Columbia drops to about 42. Start now and the winter water feels earned. Plunge always optional, current always respected. #EbbAndEmber #PortlandSauna #ColdPlunge #ColumbiaRiver

slides.headline: The river is getting colder. Good.
slides.body: Summer water sat in the 60s. By January the Columbia drops to about 42 degrees.

slides.headline: Every week it bites a little more.
slides.body: October water still feels manageable. The same jump in December feels like a different river.

slides.headline: The roof jump gets louder.
slides.body: Some guests jump off the roof. Some climb down the ladder. Both get more vocal as the water cools.

slides.headline: Snowmelt, not a chiller.
slides.body: The cold comes off the Cascades, not a thermostat. Nobody sets it. The season does.

slides.headline: The heat matters more now.
slides.body: Cedar benches around 180 degrees. On a 45 degree morning, that contrast is the whole point.

slides.headline: The plunge stays optional.
slides.body: The cold shower counts. Sitting on the ladder counts. Skipping it counts. Nobody keeps score.

slides.headline: Respect the current.
slides.body: The Columbia moves and colder water takes your breath faster. Throw rings on deck, buddy up. When in doubt, don't go out.

slides.headline: Keep your first plunge short.
slides.body: In, breathe, out. Then back to the heat. You'll know quickly how long is long enough.

slides.headline: October is the on-ramp.
slides.body: Start now and the January water feels earned instead of shocking.

slides.headline: Start your cold season this week.
slides.body: Book a social or private session at ebbandember.com. Save this for the first 42 degree day.
